title: On-demand SIG/CAIQ QA skeletons and attestation flows for contract acceleration
creator: Asha Patel
description: Deliver a minimal, reusable set of SIG/CAIQ answer skeletons (QA skeletons) plus an on-demand customer attestation flow that reduces friction during early enterprise contract cycles. The feature pairs templated answers and optional attachments with a small pricing/credit incentive to measure whether a low-touch evidence onramp shortens time-to-sign and reduces sales/legal cycles. This ticket scopes the templates, UX/Console flow, experiment variants, instrumentation, and legal/security signoffs required for a canary pilot.
acceptance_criteria: A1: A library of 20 canonical SIG/CAIQ answer skeletons (short, canonical phrasing + links to evidence) is authored, reviewed by Legal, and stored in Confluence with versioning.
A2: Console flow prototype implemented to let SEs or customers trigger 'Create Attestation Packet' that bundles selected skeletons and evidence upload links.
A3: Pricing experiment backend that issues a one-time 'attestation credit' (configurable amount) upon packet completion is implemented and gated behind feature flag.
A4: Measurement dashboard (conversion funnel, time-to-contract, legal touchpoints) is available in Looker/Grafana with baseline and experiment cohorts.
A5: Security review completed and signoff obtained from Security & Legal (security_review_required=true).
hypothesis: Providing concise, pre-reviewed SIG/CAIQ skeletons plus a low-dollar attestation credit will reduce legal Q&A back-and-forth and shorten median time-to-contract by at least 25% for mid-market customers that start in self-serve or early sales engagement.
success_metrics: Primary: 25% decrease in median time from first security request to contract signature for experiment cohort vs control (30-day window)
Secondary: 30% reduction in number of email threads with Legal per deal, 10% increase in conversion from POC to paid for cohort, and NPS uplift for onboarding experience.
Instrumentation: track events - attestation_packet_created, attestation_packet_submitted, credit_granted, contract_signed, legal_interaction_count.
rollout_plan: Step 1 (Canary): Internal pilot with 5 Sales reps + 3 enterprise customers (2/26 - 3/12)
Step 2 (Beta): Expand to 50 accounts via feature flag for 6 weeks and A/B test pricing credit variants (no credit vs $750 vs $2,500 equivalent service credit)
Step 3 (GA): Automate recurring attestation wallet + add to onboarding checklist if metrics meet success criteria
Fallback: disable credit issuance and revert to info-only packets if security/legal objections arise
notes: Trade-offs: concise skeletons reduce custom accuracy vs long-form answers; we prioritize speed over exhaustive evidence in the pilot and surface 'request more detail' flows for high-risk deals.
Design decision: Skeletons will be limited to 1-3 sentence canonical answers + 1-2 evidence links to avoid bloated attestation packets.
Quant econ: credits treated as marketing expense capped per customer; finance to model uplift threshold for full programization.
Privacy: packet storage is audit-logged and attachments are stored in S3 with ACLs mapped to the customer org; PII scanning in pipeline required before making downloadable PDFs.
